boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Southern Methodist University

cards.subtitle: 6935 Hillcrest Ave, Dallas
cards.notes: Use the Snider Plaza location for a pickup run; confirm its current hours before leaving, especially on weekends and holidays.

cards.evidence_claim: Zalat lists this Snider Plaza location open until midnight Monday–Thursday and until 4 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published hours: Mon–Thu 11 a.m.–12 a.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–4 a.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–10 p.m. Hours may change.

cards.title: Velvet Taco — Greenville

cards.title: IHOP — North Central Expressway

cards.notes: Use the official location page to check services, then choose dine-in, takeout, or online ordering for an any-hour food stop.

cards.evidence_claim: IHOP lists the 7830 N. Central Expressway restaurant as open 24 hours every day and identifies it as offering late-night food.
cards.access_notes: Published hours: open 24 hours Monday–Sunday. The location page lists late-night food, dine-in, takeout, delivery, and Wi-Fi.

cards.title: Whataburger — Haskell & Capitol

cards.access_notes: Published hours for Whataburger #728, Haskell & Capitol: open 24 hours daily; holiday hours may differ.

cards.access_notes: Published building hours: Monday–Friday 5 a.m.–9 p.m.; Saturday–Sunday 5 a.m.–7 p.m. Dining access may depend on SMU eligibility.

cards.title: Hughes-Trigg Student Center

cards.title: Dedman Center for Lifetime Sports

cards.title: Bridwell Library
cards.subtitle: SMU campus, Dallas

cards.short_summary: A city park with a rubberized track, outdoor fitness area, and lighted tennis court.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of University Park identifies Germany Park at 6401 Lomo Alto Drive and describes its rubberized track, outdoor fitness area, and lighted tennis court.
cards.source_title: City of University Park — Germany Park
cards.access_notes: Follow the city’s posted track lane guidance; court access and lighting may be subject to city rules.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented SMU rituals and recurring celebrations, from Dallas Hall ceremonies to Mustang game-day customs.

cards.title: Walk the Rotunda Passage
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation and May Baccalaureate • Dallas Hall
cards.notes: Notice the two directions of the ritual: new students enter through Dallas Hall, while graduating students make their final campus walk out.
cards.short_summary: Dallas Hall frames both the formal welcome to SMU and the symbolic departure at graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU identifies the Rotunda Passage as a symbolic tradition comprising a processional for entering students and a recessional for graduates.
cards.access_notes: Occurs within scheduled Opening Convocation and Baccalaureate ceremonies; ceremony participation is directed by SMU.

cards.title: Pass the Howard Lantern
cards.subtitle: May Baccalaureate Service
cards.notes: Look for the lantern handoff from the senior class president to a junior-class representative during the May Baccalaureate Service.
cards.short_summary: A lantern handoff represents the continuing light of learning between SMU classes.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU states that the Howard Lantern is handed annually at May Baccalaureate from the senior class president to a junior-class representative.
cards.access_notes: Presented during SMU's scheduled May Baccalaureate Service.

cards.title: Watch the Ovilla Curtain Fall
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation • McFarlin Auditorium
cards.notes: At the close of Opening Convocation, watch for the historic curtain to lower—the ceremonial signal that the new class's initiation is complete.
cards.short_summary: A historic McFarlin Auditorium fire curtain closes SMU's formal welcome for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU says the Ovilla Curtain is lowered at the end of Opening Convocation to signify completion of new students' initiation.
cards.access_notes: Part of the scheduled Opening Convocation ceremony in McFarlin Auditorium.

cards.title: Sing “Varsity” at the Close
cards.subtitle: Convocation, Baccalaureate, and athletics
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before a major campus ceremony or game, then join the community when “Varsity” is sung at the close.
cards.short_summary: SMU's 1916 alma mater links academic ceremonies and sporting events.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU describes “Varsity” as its official school song, sung at Opening Convocation, December Commencement, Baccalaureate, and sporting events.
cards.access_notes: Presented at scheduled university ceremonies and athletics events.

cards.title: Make the Pony Ears
cards.subtitle: SMU spirit gesture • campus events and games
cards.notes: Start with a peace sign, relax the first two fingers slightly, and use the gesture in photos, cheers, and school-song moments.
cards.short_summary: SMU's hand sign turns a relaxed two-finger gesture into pony ears.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU instructs students to form Pony Ears with a relaxed peace sign and says the symbol is used for photos, cheering, and school songs.
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: A spirit gesture used at campus occasions; follow event guidance where applicable.

cards.title: Boulevard Before Kickoff
cards.subtitle: Bishop Boulevard • SMU home football games
cards.notes: Before a home game, walk Bishop Boulevard and Dallas Hall Lawn to take in the established pregame gathering known as Boulevarding.
cards.short_summary: At SMU, the pre-football-game gathering has its own verb: Boulevarding.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU describes Boulevarding as its home-football-game tradition, with the community gathering along Bishop Boulevard and Dallas Hall Lawn.
cards.source_title: Experience Campus Life at SMU | SMU
cards.access_notes: Takes place before scheduled SMU home football games; follow current game-day and venue guidance.

cards.title: See the Pigskin Revue
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Weekend
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming program for the variety show, where student groups, faculty, alumni, and the Mustang Band take the stage.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming variety show has brought SMU community acts together since 1933.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU calls Pigskin Revue its longest-running tradition and says the Homecoming variety show began in 1933.
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: Presented during scheduled Homecoming Weekend programming; consult the current event program.

cards.title: Celebrate PerunaPalooza
cards.subtitle: Spring • Peruna's birthday celebration
cards.notes: Find the spring birthday festival for SMU's live mascot, then spend time with its games, rides, and campus activities.
cards.short_summary: SMU marks its mascot Peruna's birthday with a spring festival.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU states that PerunaPalooza is held every spring to celebrate Peruna's birthday and includes games, rides, and activities.
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: A spring event; confirm the current date, location, and entry details with SMU programming.

cards.title: Wait for Dallas Hall to Light Up
cards.subtitle: Holiday season • Dallas Hall Lawn
cards.notes: Gather on the Dallas Hall lawn for student carols, then stay through “Silent Night” for the lighting of the building.
cards.short_summary: Dallas Hall's holiday illumination is the finale of SMU's seasonal community gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU says Celebration of Lights gathers the community for carols and concludes with the lighting of Dallas Hall after “Silent Night.”
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: A holiday-season event; verify the current program details before attending.

cards.title: Spot the “Diamond M”
cards.subtitle: SMU football game performances
cards.notes: At a football game, watch the Mustang Band's field presentation for its documented “Diamond M” formation and feature twirler.
cards.short_summary: The Mustang Band's signature field formation turns the SMU initial into a diamond-shaped M.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU identifies the Mustang Band's “Diamond M” formation as part of its spirit-and-traditions presentation.
cards.access_notes: Seen during scheduled football-game band performances; stadium entry and viewing follow current event rules.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Southern Methodist University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-stakes first-weekend loop through SMU’s academic, student-life, arts, recreation, dining, and campus gathering spaces.

cards.title: Start with the rotunda
cards.subtitle: Friday morning · Dallas Hall, 3225 University Boulevard
cards.notes: Walk through the main doors, pause beneath the rotunda, and use the landmark as your first visual anchor before exploring the rest of campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin at SMU’s flagship historic building and orient yourself from the Hilltop.
cards.evidence_claim: Dallas Hall is SMU’s first building and a historic landmark; every undergraduate student crosses through its rotunda.
cards.access_notes: Academic and office building; follow posted building-access guidance.

cards.title: Choose a study perch at Fondren
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 6414 Robert S. Hyer Lane
cards.notes: Make a short first-weekend study plan, then choose an open seating area that matches your noise preference before classes begin in earnest.
cards.short_summary: Find a practical campus workspace in SMU’s main library.
cards.evidence_claim: Fondren Library is SMU’s main library, and its Collaborative Commons has tables, booths, monitors, and a Starbucks Cafe.
cards.access_notes: Open study spaces do not require reservations; guests are welcome during public access hours.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Hughes-Trigg
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 3140 Dyer Street
cards.notes: Walk the public areas, identify the student-services offices you may need later, and make this your regrouping point for the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Use SMU’s student-center hub to locate everyday campus resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Hughes-Trigg was redesigned as a gathering space where students socialize, study, and participate in campus opportunities.
cards.source_title: SMU Hughes-Trigg Student Center - Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Student-center office hours are Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; building access may vary.

cards.title: Share a first campus meal
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Umphrey Lee Center, 3300 Dyer Street
cards.notes: Meet a classmate or roommate for a meal, compare the available stations, and use the conversation to plan one simple activity for Saturday.
cards.short_summary: Put a shared meal into the first-weekend schedule at a campus dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU lists Umphrey Lee as a campus dining hall with all-you-can-eat access for students and regular-term dining hours.
cards.access_notes: Dining-hall access uses an SMU meal plan; regular-term hours vary by day.

cards.title: Spend Saturday with Spanish art
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 5900 Bishop Boulevard
cards.notes: Check the gallery hours, pick a few works to discuss with a friend, and leave time to browse without trying to see every room.
cards.short_summary: Visit SMU’s on-campus art museum for a self-paced cultural stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Meadows Museum is at 5900 Bishop Boulevard and admission is free for SMU students.
cards.access_notes: Hours: Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday until 9 p.m.; Sunday 1–5 p.m. Closed Monday.

cards.title: Try a low-pressure rec session
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · 6000 Bush Avenue
cards.notes: Choose one activity that feels approachable—walking the track, shooting baskets, or checking the climbing wall—and learn the facility layout together.
cards.short_summary: Use SMU Campus Recreation for an active, alcohol-free Saturday evening.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dedman Center has courts, an indoor track, climbing walls, pools, fitness areas, and other recreation spaces.
cards.source_title: SMU Dedman Center for Lifetime Sports - Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open to enrolled SMU students and members; fall/spring building hours run as late as 11 p.m. on select days.

cards.title: See the stadium from Bush Avenue
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · 5801 Bush Avenue
cards.notes: Walk by the stadium exterior, note its location relative to the residential side of campus, and save event attendance for a ticketed date that fits you.
cards.short_summary: Locate SMU’s football stadium as part of an easy campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Gerald J. Ford Stadium is at 5801 Bush Avenue and has a 32,000-seat horseshoe configuration.
cards.source_title: Gerald J. Ford Stadium - SMU Facilities
cards.access_notes: View from public campus routes; entry to games or events requires the applicable ticket and venue rules.

cards.title: Pause at Perkins Chapel
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Charles and Elizabeth Prothro Theology Quadrangle
cards.notes: Take a quiet exterior walk around the quadrangle, notice the chapel’s Georgian details, and check the calendar before attending any worship or recital.
cards.short_summary: Build in a reflective stop at a prominent SMU chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Perkins Chapel is SMU’s primary worship setting and also serves as a venue for private devotions, holy-day celebrations, and recitals.
cards.source_title: Perkins Chapel: A Chapel for the 21st Century | SMU Perkins School of Theology
cards.access_notes: The chapel hosts worship and other scheduled activities; confirm availability before entering.

cards.title: Check what is on at McFarlin
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 6405 Boaz Lane
cards.notes: Look at the upcoming calendar, then choose a future performance or talk that interests you rather than trying to fill every first-weekend hour.
cards.short_summary: Get familiar with a historic performance venue and its event calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: McFarlin Memorial Auditorium is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and hosts performances by vocalists, comedians, bands, and dance companies.
cards.access_notes: Event access and ticket requirements vary; consult the listing for the specific program.

cards.title: Finish in the arts complex
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 6101 Bishop Boulevard
cards.notes: Walk the building’s public areas, note the galleries and performance spaces, and pick one future screening, exhibit, or performance to revisit.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend by mapping SMU’s dance, music, theatre, and visual-arts home.
cards.evidence_claim: Owen Arts Center contains dance, music, and theatre spaces, galleries, studios, and public performance venues.
cards.source_title: Owen Arts Center - Meadows School of the Arts, SMU
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on gallery and performance schedules; check the relevant event or gallery information.
